findings.title: Pre-registration says Gmail documents are 'about the ticket', but no Gmail document in the 5,000 mentions the ticket or PR; the hazard hit 1 of 2 questions
findings.evidence: pr_issue-due_date-127 asks about PR #193, which links ENG-4821. At 5k, v9, v11 and v13 all plan 'reviewers → mailbox_owner_of [gmail] → first_email_at → earliest', and v12 and v14 plan '... → label → list'. No Gmail document in the 5,000 mentions ENG-4821 or #193 (regex with word boundaries). The PR's four reviewers are named in 135, 63, 18 and 2 Gmail documents. So the plan reaches Gmail through the reviewers' mailboxes, not through Gmail about the ticket, which is what the pre-reg's line 162 describes ('at 5,000 there are Gmail documents about the ticket'). The pre-freeze review raised the same point. Two of the 50 questions drew the 'status email' wording; the other, pr_issue-due_date-070 on planted PR #43678, was answered correctly at 5k through linked_linear.
findings.implication: 'At 5,000 the plan ends at Gmail' is accurate. The write-up should describe the actual path (the PR's reviewers' mailboxes) and say the hazard fired on 1 of the 2 questions with that wording, rather than reuse the pre-registration's 'Gmail documents about the ticket' explanation.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this finding and could not. Every claim checks out against the saved data, using light CPU only.
(1) Plans: answers_md5k/factbank_v9, v11 and v13 all give 'Add sales demo app ... → reviewers → mailbox_owner_of [gmail] → first_email_at → earliest' for pr_issue-due_date-127. v12 and v14 give '... → mailbox_owner_of [gmail] → label → list'. On the small bank, v13 plans '→ linked_linear → due_date → single' and gets 2025-11-12.
(2) No Gmail mention: I mapped the 5,000 dsids in haystack_5k.json to files through mt5k/index.json and searched all 1,188 Gmail documents. None matches \bENG-4821\b, '#193', 'PR 193' or \b193\b, and none mentions 'Optimization Config' or 'redwood-examples'. Across all sources, '#193' appears nowhere and \b193\b appears only in the PR itself and in one Slack finance document.
(3) Reviewer counts: the four reviewers (Monica Patel, Markus Klein, Alex Martinez, Elliot Price) are named in exactly 135, 63, 18 and 2 Gmail documents. The wrong answer v13 gave, 'Scheduling: SOC 2 / DPA walkthrough for FinovateX', comes from gmail/alex_martinez/..., which is a reviewer's mailbox. So the plan reached Gmail through the reviewers' mailboxes, not through any Gmail document about the ticket.
(4) Pre-registration line 162 does say 'at 5,000 there are Gmail documents about the ticket'. prefreeze_review_a.json has a protocol-lens finding that raised the same point before the freeze.
(5) questions.jsonl has 50 questions, and exactly 2 use the 'status email' wording: 127 and 070. 070's PR (dsid_05bdc...) is in draw_report's planted list, and v13 answered it correctly at 5,000 (2025-03-01, through linked_linear). So the hazard hit 1 of 2.
The write-up has not been committed yet (HEAD 6266c34 says 'write-up and review to follow'), so this is advice on how to describe the cause, not an error already published. It changes no score, rule or verdict. Scratch scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/post5ka/gmail127.py and mbox.py.

findings.title: Review exposure is slightly larger than disclosed for planted pairs, and two test questions were answered word for word in review
findings.evidence: 6 of the 10 planted pairs (both documents) appear in at least one pre-freeze review draw (rev5ka big101, big202, big7, d997 and others). The pre-registration says 'about 4 or 5'. Only 2 pairs (planted #3 and #9) had a review question answered on them (rev5ka/small7, sym7). Two of the 50 test questions were answered verbatim in review: issue_pr_author-author-071 (v1, v4 and v13 in rev5ka/small7 and sym7) and person_first-048 (v4, v8, v9, v11 and v13 in rev5ka/pfprobe). Six test questions appear word for word in review folders' question files. 18 of the 105 small-set documents are in some review draw. The code and lessons were not changed after the review.
findings.implication: This does not bias the frozen system's scores. The disclosure should say 6 of 10 planted pairs were present in review draws (2 with questions asked), and name the 2 test questions answered verbatim in review (v13 gets both right on both banks).

verdict.reason:
Most of the counts check out, but one claim is overstated. I worked from the saved data only (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/post5ka/refute_rev/).

Confirmed:
- Every rev5ka review haystack was made before the freeze (07:39 to 08:18, freeze at 08:30:08). Counting the test's planted pairs (draw_report.json) with both documents in a saved review haystack gives {1,2,3,7,8,9}: 6 of 10. big7 holds 3 and 9, big101 holds 9, big202 holds 1 and 2, and inlink/d997 holds 2, 3, 7 and 8 (only one side of 9). Pairs 1, 2, 3 and 9 were planted in the review draws themselves (big7, big101, big202 draw_report.json).
- The pre-registration says 'about 4 or 5'. The pre-freeze verifier in prefreeze_review_a.json had estimated 10 x 31/56, about 5.5 (simulated mean 5.6), so 6 is slightly above both.
- Only pairs 3 and 9 had a review question answered on both their documents: pr_issue-status-149 and issue_pr_author-author-082 in small7 and sym7. Pair 8 was touched only on one side, by a pfprobe person_first question.
- 6 of the 50 test questions match a review questions.jsonl word for word.
- 18 of the 105 small-set documents are in some rev5ka haystack.
- Between review and freeze, the only code change was factbank_5k.py (draw, pick and eval). No bank, planner or lesson code changed.
- v13 answers issue_pr_author-author-071 and person_first-048 correctly on both banks.

Overstated: 'two test questions were answered verbatim in review' is true of the wording only.
- issue_pr_author-author-071 really is the same question: same gold documents and expected answer (Ava Martinez) as review author-082 in big7 and small7, answered there by v1, v4 and v13.
- person_first-048 ('Of all the tickets assigned to Marco Rivera, which one is due first?') matches pfprobe's s202-person_first-002 in words only. The gold documents differ and do not overlap, the expected answer differs (ENG-37042 in review, ENG-991234 in the test), and none of 048's gold documents were in the pfprobe bank. The review never answered the test question's substance.
- Of the six word-for-word matches, only two have the same gold documents and expected answer: 071 and issue_pr_author-author-097. 097 sits in inlink/d997's questions.jsonl but was never answered.

So the disclosure should say:
- 6 of 10 planted pairs were in review draws, with questions answered on 2 of them;
- one test question (071) was answered in review in the same form;
- another (097) was drawn in review but not answered;
- 048 matches only in wording, on different documents.

The finding itself says this does not move any score or verdict, and I agree.

findings.title: The 5,000-document bank hashes cannot be verified now, and bank_sha256.txt does not name its files
findings.evidence: md5k/*.sqlite no longer exist, so the md5kx symlinks dangle. part_a/bank_sha256.txt holds two bare 16-hex prefixes (2c7aa6b3e9c46b7a, d15d4d9e83fa6c26) with no filenames. Rebuilding was out of scope under the CPU limit. Build records match: md5k/factbank 95,350,784 bytes, 97,447 facts; factbank_v2 103,288,832 bytes, 116,132 facts; 14,100 entities. The small banks are kept, but their hashes (06a86a22c522ec0f, 5d195c035273a67c) are not recorded in part_a.
findings.implication: Label which hash belongs to which bank, add the small banks' hashes, and once part B finishes, rebuild md5k once to confirm the build is deterministic.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on every point; I could not refute any of it. (1) The 5,000-document banks are gone. md5k/ has no .sqlite files left, so md5kx/factbank.sqlite and md5kx/factbank_v2.sqlite point at files that no longer exist. Only the two *_build.json links in md5kx still resolve. (2) cie/docs/benchmarks/factbank_5k/part_a/bank_sha256.txt holds just two bare 16-hex prefixes, 2c7aa6b3e9c46b7a and d15d4d9e83fa6c26, with no filenames. Nothing else in cie/docs, cie/src, the run log or the commit message says which prefix goes with which bank; a grep found the prefixes only in that file. run_5k.sh does not compute bank hashes at all: its sha256sum line covers haystack.json, questions.jsonl, the small haystack and the set-aside questions (e18bc400…, 7162dc9a…, 0e572c3b…, ba89a71d… in the log). So the bank file was written by hand outside the pre-registered script, and how it was made is not on record. (3) The build records match what the finding says: md5k factbank has 97,447 facts and 95,350,784 bytes, factbank_v2 has 116,132 facts and 103,288,832 bytes, both with 14,100 entities. (4) The small banks hash to 06a86a22c522ec0f and 5d195c035273a67c, and neither prefix appears anywhere in part_a. One thing I added: I rebuilt the small bank under post5ka/detcheck (about 1 second each, PYTHONHASHSEED=0) and got byte-identical files with the same two hashes. So the build is deterministic at small size, and the finding's suggestion of rebuilding md5k once part B is done would work. Impact: this is a provenance and labelling gap only. The pre-registration does not require bank hashes, and all scores come from saved answer files, so the 'all 5 rules met' result does not depend on it. Severity low.

findings.title: Draw reproduces byte for byte, and its rules hold when checked independently
findings.evidence: I re-ran factbank_5k.build_sets (seeds 53/54, same exclusions) into post5ka/redraw. haystack.json (e18bc400f741f4e2), questions.jsonl (7162dc9a2dde432e), the small haystack (0e572c3b82cc2d36), the set-aside questions (ba89a71dab727209) and draw_report.json are all identical to md5k and to the hashes in the log. findings.title: The 'status email' loss is a systematic hazard, not a one-off: with only the Gmail documents the 5,000 set really holds, 10 of the 11 asked-about PRs fail on that wording
findings.evidence: The wording appeared twice: pr_issue-due_date-127 (PR #193) was lost and pr_issue-due_date-070 (PR #43678) survived. I ran the review's field-level reach probe (rev5ka/emailprobe/reach_all.py) on the md5k haystack. It found 72 of 77 PRs reach Gmail within 2 hops, and 10 of the 11 PRs in the questions do. PR #43678 is the only one with 0 Gmail paths. So 070 survived because of its data. I built two small banks: post5ka/emailctl (the 105-document small set) and post5ka/emailbank (the same set plus the 274 Gmail documents the 11 PRs reach). I asked frozen v13 'When is the ticket linked to pull request #N due? I need the deadline date for the status email.' for all 11 PRs. emailctl: 11 of 11 right. emailbank: 1 of 11 right, and the one is #43678. The plans were '-> reviewers/author -> participants_external_of [gmail] -> first_email_at' for the planted PRs, and for #193 '-> reviewers -> mailbox_owner_of [gmail] -> first_email_at -> earliest'. That is the same plan as in the real 5k run, and #43678 gives the same right plan as in the real run. The small set holds only Linear (86), GitHub (11) and Fireflies (8), so the control can never show this hazard.
findings.implication: The write-up should not say 'one question lost to size' without context. It should say that any question naming a system in passing is routed to that system whenever a path exists, and at 5,000 documents a path almost always exists. This draw happened to show it once. The verdict holds anyway: had 070 also failed, v13 would be 0.952, -0.032 against the small bank, so rules 1 and 2 would still be met. But the margin is about 3 link questions (0.016 each), and the dry run lost exactly 3.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. Every concrete claim checks out against the saved data and the frozen code. The source in cie/src is unchanged between 7dae3b8 and HEAD.

(1) Only two questions use the wording: questions.jsonl has 'status email' in pr_issue-due_date-127 (PR #193) and pr_issue-due_date-070 (PR #43678).

(2) I re-ran rev5ka/emailprobe/reach_all.py on the md5k haystack. It reads structured fields only and took about 3 seconds under nice. It printed 'prs': 77, 'reach gmail': 72. Ten of the 11 PRs in the questions have Gmail paths within 2 hops, and #43678 has none (gmail paths {}). For #193 the paths are reviewers->participants_internal_of (247) and reviewers->mailbox_owner_of (40). For the planted PRs they are reviewers/author->participants_external_of.

(3) I scored the saved answers in post5ka/emailctl/factbank_v13.jsonl (105 documents) and post5ka/emailbank/factbank_v13.jsonl (379 documents = the small set plus the reachable Gmail documents). emailctl gets 11 of 11, all via 'linked_linear -> due_date'. emailbank gets 1 of 11, and the one right answer is #43678. The other ten plans end at '[gmail] -> first_email_at' (one gives 'region' instead). For #193 the plan is 'reviewers -> mailbox_owner_of [gmail] -> first_email_at -> earliest'. That matches answers_md5k/factbank_v13.jsonl from the real run exactly. In both banks #43678 gets the right 'linked_linear -> due_date' plan, as in the real run.

(4) The code makes this deterministic, not a sampling accident. In engine.SYSTEM_WORDS, 'email' maps to gmail. plans.target_system picks the first named system the starts do not belong to: gmail for a PR start, because 'ticket' is added last. Check rule 2 (other_system) keeps only plans ending in that system whenever any plan passes. The later rules are skipped rather than undoing rule 2. candidates() lists every 2-hop path with no cap. So the full 5,000 bank, which holds these Gmail documents and more, would route the same way. I did not re-answer on that bank, as instructed.

(5) The arithmetic is right. Link scores 19 of 21 at 5,000. If 070 also failed, link would be 18/21 = 0.857 and the mean (0.857 + 1 + 1)/3 = 0.952. That is -0.032 against 0.984, which still clears rule 1 (>= 0.934) and rule 2 (>= 0.92). Each link question is worth about 0.016, so three more link losses would break rule 1.

What is already disclosed: FACTBANK_5K_PREREGISTRATION.md and dry_run.json describe the mechanism. The dry run lost all three status-email questions (127, 132, 158). What is new in the finding: 070 survived only because PR #43678 has no Gmail path, and when the wording is drawn about 10 of 11 such PRs would fail. That makes 'one question lost to size' and the preregistration's 'may or may not draw that wording' understate the hazard. The severity is overstated, because no verdict changes.

findings.title: Pre-registration's Gmail mechanism is wrong for this run: no Gmail document mentions the lost ticket
findings.evidence: FACTBANK_5K_PREREGISTRATION.md lines 162 and 194 say there are Gmail documents about the ticket at 5,000. PR #193 links ENG-4821, and ENG-4821 appears in no Gmail document of the 5,000. It appears only in 6 Drive, 3 Linear and 2 GitHub documents. No question PR number is mentioned in any other document. The v13 journal goes through #193's reviewers: Monica Patel (owner of 8 threads, internal participant in 157), Markus Klein (15/70) and Alex Martinez (16/18). The pre-freeze review flagged this wording ('names the wrong route'), but the frozen text still says 'about the ticket'. The sentence 'the test set may or may not draw that wording' also leaves out the second condition: whether the PR's people reach Gmail.
findings.implication: The results write-up should correct the mechanism: the planner reaches Gmail through the pull request's people (mailbox owners, internal participants, and namesake external participants), not through documents about the ticket.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. Every claim that matters checks out against the data and saved answers. All work was light: text scans of the 5,000 source JSON files and reading saved files, with scripts in scratchpad/post5ka/.

1. **No Gmail document mentions the ticket.** PR #193 (github/redwood-examples/pr-193-...json) has linked_linear ['PM-197', 'ENG-4821']. A regex scan of the 5,000 documents listed in part_a/haystack_5k.json found ENG-4821 in 15 files: 6 Linear, 6 Drive and 3 GitHub, counting the two gold documents. None is Gmail. Without the gold documents that is 5 Linear, 6 Drive and 2 GitHub. The reviewer's '3 Linear' differs from my count, but that does not affect the claim.
   - None of the 1,188 Gmail documents mentions PM-197, 'Optimization Config', 'config version' or 'sales demo app' either. So no Gmail document is about the ticket even loosely.
   - The ENG-4821 Linear document has no linked_gmail_threads field.
   - Neither PR number named in the questions (193, 43678) appears as #N, pull/N or PR N in any document.
2. **The route is through the PR's reviewers.** In part_a/answers_md5k/factbank_v13.jsonl, v13's saved reason for pr_issue-due_date-127 is 'Add sales demo app ... → reviewers → mailbox_owner_of [gmail] → first_email_at → earliest'. Its answer is an email subject ('Scheduling: SOC 2 / DPA walkthrough for FinovateX'). The people it read are Markus Klein, Alex Martinez, Elliot Price and Monica Patel, which are exactly the PR's reviewers.
3. **The reviewer counts match exactly.** I recounted the Gmail mailbox_owner and participants_internal fields:
   - Monica Patel: owner of 8, internal participant in 157.
   - Markus Klein: 15 and 70.
   - Alex Martinez: 16 and 18.
4. **The pre-freeze review did flag this, and the text was not changed.** In docs/benchmarks/factbank_5k/prefreeze_review_a.json, the item "The 'status email' disclosure describes mt5k, not this draw" ends in a verdict saying the phrase 'Gmail documents about the ticket' 'names the wrong route'. It describes the route as PR → reviewers or author → mailbox_owner_of or participants_internal_of. The pre-registration file is unmodified since commit 7dae3b8, and lines 162 and 194 still say 'about the ticket'. 'The test set may or may not draw that wording' names only one of the two conditions.

**What I could not refute or confirm:**
- Line 194 describes the dry run on mt5k, where a few PRs may have reached Gmail through the ticket. I could not find the dry run's questions to check. Line 162, though, is a general claim 'at 5,000', and it is false for the question this run lost.
- I did not check the 'namesake external participants' detail.

findings.title: 50 questions are about 42 independent checks; PR questions sit almost entirely on hand-planted, structurally clean pairs
findings.evidence: Of 125 gold-document slots, 105 are distinct, and 19 gold documents serve more than one question. Linked through shared gold documents, the 50 questions form 42 clusters (sizes 3, 2x6, 1x35). ENG-7610 (Liam Patel) carries person_first-006, action_owner_issues-092 and issue_pr_author-097. Maya Chen is the subject of -110 and -084 and the answer of -097. Daniel Kim, Diego Ruiz and PRs 274801, 43678 and 60921 each carry 2. 22 person questions cover 18 people. 14 PR questions cover 11 PRs, and 13 of those questions are on the 10 planted pairs. Each planted pair's ticket is referenced by no other PR, and the PR's other linked tickets are kept out, so a second reading is impossible by construction. Only pr_issue-due_date-127 (PR #193, not planted) came from a natural PR, and it is the one lost.
findings.implication: The write-up should report clusters, not just 50. It should say plainly that PR-anchored link questions test the easiest form (one PR, one ticket in the bank), and that PRs linking several tickets in the bank were engineered out of the decisive score.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the numbers, but the "engineered out" part is overstated and the verdict does not change.

Checked against part_a/questions.jsonl and draw_report.json:
- **Gold documents:** 125 slots, 105 distinct, 19 shared by more than one question.
- **Clusters:** questions linked through shared gold documents form 42 clusters (one of 3, six of 2, 35 single), as claimed.
- **ENG-7610:** carries person_first-006, action_owner_issues-092 and issue_pr_author-author-097.
- **Repeats:** Daniel Kim (038, 089), Diego Ruiz (045, 152), PR 274801 (125, 126), PR 43678 (070, 071) and PR 60921 (113, 114) each carry 2. Maya Chen is the subject of 110 and 084 and the answer of 097.
- **People:** the 22 person questions cover 18 people.
- **PRs:** the 14 PR questions cover 11 PRs. All 10 planted PRs appear, with 13 questions on them. Only pr_issue-due_date-127 (PR #193) is not planted, and it is the one lost.

Why it is still a real point:
- The pre-registration already discloses the planting rule (one Linear issue no other PR references, the PR's other tickets kept out). It also says qualitatively that the questions share documents and are "fewer than 50 independent checks".
- It does not give the 42-cluster count. It also does not say that 13 of the 14 PR questions sit on planted pairs.
- The reported summary gives neither.
- So asking the write-up to report clusters, and to state that PR link questions are almost all planted one-PR, one-ticket pairs, is a fair, concrete request.

What is overstated:
- **Nothing was removed in this draw.** The rule that keeps a planted PR's other tickets out skipped 0 documents (the only skip reason recorded is 'ticket key already drawn': 3). No PR question was set aside as "linked" (linked: ticket_link 2 only).
- **The natural PRs are just as clean.** I read the 77 GitHub documents in the set. The three natural PRs that link a ticket in the set (19857, 311, 193) each link exactly one: ENG-4821. No PR in the 5,000-document bank, planted or natural, links more than one ticket in the bank.
- **#193's loss is not about a second ticket.** At 5,000, v13's plan went from the PR to its reviewers, then to their Gmail mailboxes, then to the first email date ("PR → reviewers → mailbox_owner_of [gmail] → first_email_at"). That is the "status email" hazard disclosed in the dry run. The planted question pr_issue-due_date-070 has the same "status email" wording and was right on both banks.

The verdict holds when scored by cluster:
- **Rules 1 and 2:** v13 goes from 0.976 on the small bank to 0.952 at 5,000 (−0.024, within −0.05; above 0.92).
- **Rule 4:** v14 also goes from 0.976 to 0.952.
- **Rule 3:** at 5,000, v9 0.874, v4 0.548, v8 0.706, so v9 leads v4 by 0.33 and v8 by 0.17.

No rule changes. This is a reporting and meaning issue for the write-up, not a change to the result. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/post5ka/ (clusters.py and prs.py).

findings.title: Names are merged across internal staff and external contacts, which creates new routes at 5,000
findings.evidence: Gmail participants_external includes 'Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@devspark.com>', 'Maya Chen <mchen@nyxsys.com>', 'Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nyxsys.com>' and 'Marco Ruiz <marco@euvendor.com>'. These names are also internal engineers who are PR authors or reviewers or question subjects (Evan Brooks is the subject of action_owner_issues-120). The reach probe shows the planted PRs reach Gmail only through participants_external_of, so person identity is by name alone. None of the decisive questions failed because of this.
findings.implication: This is the 'names that match several people' hazard appearing as structural links, not as question wording. It should be listed as a limit, because it fed the email failures in the probe.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every factual claim checks out against the data and the code, so it stands as a low-severity limit that changes no verdict.

1. **Names are merged by name alone.** In the code, src/cie/ingest/sources.py person_name() removes the '<email>' part. src/cie/factbank/bank.py add_document() then keys every person field to person_key(name) and adds a '{field}_of' inverse fact. An external Gmail contact and an internal engineer with the same name therefore become one entity.

2. **The four names are confirmed.** In the 5,000 documents (docs5k.pkl), these exact Gmail participants_external strings exist: 'Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@devspark.com>', 'Maya Chen <mchen@nyxsys.com>', 'Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nyxsys.com>' (plus 3 other domains) and 'Marco Ruiz <marco@euvendor.com>' (plus 2 others). None of the four appears in Gmail as a mailbox_owner or as an internal participant. All four are GitHub authors or reviewers:
   - Aisha Patel authored the planted PRs 119842, 274801 and 60921.
   - Maya Chen authored the planted PRs 998823 and 421309.
   - Marco Ruiz reviewed PRs 119842 and 60921.
   - Evan Brooks is a Linear assignee. In action_owner_issues-120 he owns the action item (as 'Evan Brooks (Security Architect)', a customer attendee), and the expected answer is the Linear tickets assigned to Evan Brooks.

3. **The planted PRs reach Gmail only through external participants.** I checked the author and reviewers of all 10 planted PRs. Every one who appears in Gmail at all appears only in participants_external, so within two links a planted PR reaches Gmail only through participants_external_of.

4. **This route caused the probe's failures.** In post5ka/emailbank, each PR's question was reworded to the 'status email' form, on the small set plus the Gmail documents those PRs reach. v13 got 10 of 11 wrong. 9 of the 10 plans run author or reviewers → participants_external_of [gmail]. The control (post5ka/emailctl) answers all 11 right. So the name merge is what makes those Gmail routes exist.

5. **No decisive result fails because of this, as the finding says.** In the real test, pr_issue-due_date-127 went through 'reviewers → mailbox_owner_of [gmail]'. PR 193 is a natural PR, not a planted one. Its reviewers Monica Patel, Markus Klein, Alex Martinez and Elliot Price really are internal mailbox owners (for example monica.patel@redwood.com), so that loss is the disclosed 'status email' hazard and not a namesake merge.

**Partial mitigation:** merging people by name is already known. understand.json says the bank merges namesakes and that 116 of 394 internal tracker names are also used for external contacts. FACTBANK_MULTI_RESULTS.md:178 has a similar case, and the pre-registration lists 'names that match several people' under what size can still break. What is new is that the merge also creates the links the planner follows to Gmail at 5,000. The write-up, which is still to come, should list that as a limit.

**Effect on results:** the scores, all 5 rules and the hash-seed result are unchanged.

My checking scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/post5ka/ext_refute/ (a.py, b.py, c.py).

findings.title: The miss on both banks (ticket_link-assignee-067) is a self-link defect, independent of size, affecting about 5% of tickets
findings.evidence: The `links` field of ENG-96111 contains 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-sequencer/tree/ENG-96111'. The bank turns that into a link to itself. v13's plan '-> links -> assignee -> single' reaches doc ENG-96111 and answers its own assignee, Riley Kapoor. The expected answer comes from parent_issue ENG-61234 (Miguel Rivera). The journal is identical on both banks. In the 5,000 set, 19 of 400 tickets have a followed field whose key is their own: links 11, attachments 6, related_links 1, related_confluence_pages 1. why_unclear's 'linked' check excludes the ticket itself, so these are not set aside.
findings.implication: The write-up should name this as a bank bug, not a size effect. Branch URLs named after the ticket are common in real repositories, so it would recur on ticket-link questions.

verdict.reason:
The facts in the finding check out, but its main claim does not. Removing the self-link does not fix the answer.

What checks out:
(1) The `links` field of ENG-96111 contains https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-sequencer/tree/ENG-96111. In md5ksmall/factbank_v2.sqlite, fact dsid_00cf...#29 (links) has value_entity = the document itself. Fact #30 is a referenced_by self-fact. The cause is in cie/src/cie/factbank/bank.py add_document: it sets target = key:<first reference key> and never drops the ticket's own key. cie/src/cie/ingest/sources.py does drop it (`if k not in own`).
(2) v13's journal on both banks is identical: the plan '-> links -> assignee -> single' reaches doc:dsid_00cf... plus three page identifiers, and it answers Riley Kapoor.
(3) My recount (post5ka/selflinks.py) gives 19 of 400 tickets (linear 341 + jira 59) whose followed fields cite their own key: links 11, attachments 6, related_links 1, related_confluence_pages 1.
(4) _second_link in factbank_5k.py skips `_key(d) in (k, target)`, so the ticket itself is never counted as a second reading.

What fails: I re-answered the question with v13 (plans mdtrain/plan_lessons_v13.json, lessons fb50/lessons.json) on two copies of the small bank:
- post5ka/sl067_orig, unchanged: answers Riley Kapoor through the links plan, as in the run.
- post5ka/sl067_fixed: fact #29's value_entity set to NULL and fact #30 deleted, which is what the bank would hold if it dropped own keys the way sources.py does. v13 still answers Riley Kapoor, now through '-> assignee -> label -> single'.

In the fixed copy the parent_issue plan that gives Miguel Rivera is only third, behind two plans that read ENG-96111's own assignee. The original run's runner-up plans also all answered Riley Kapoor. So the self-link only decides which wrong plan wins. The miss comes from the planner ranking 'read this ticket's own assignee' above 'parent_issue -> assignee' for 'linked ticket'. Calling it a self-link defect is wrong as the cause of the miss.

On the implication: the report never treats 067 as a size loss. It says v13 misses it on both banks, and rule 1's only size loss is pr_issue-due_date-127, so no rule outcome changes. The self-link inconsistency is a real but separate latent issue. It is worth a note, but it did not cause this miss.

findings.title: Timing: 6.6 s is under 7-way contention; v13 alone takes about 4 s at 5k. The cost is repeated uncached alias scans and grows with the bank
findings.evidence: run_5k.sh runs 7 arms at once on 4 cores. v13 (seed 0) ran alongside them: median 6,563 ms, p90 10,379, total 358 s. The seed-1 v13 rerun ran alone after all other arms: median 4,061 ms, p90 6,529, max 7,946. v14's 4.3 s ran mostly alone (08:40:36 to 08:44:16), so it does not show the form is faster. I instrumented FactBank.named on a 379-document bank: 8 calls per question, 68% of ask time (5.9 of 8.6 s). named() runs one re.search per alias (engine.py:124), and Python 3.12's regex cache holds only 512 patterns. Measured cost per alias was 7.5 us at 304 aliases and 72 us at 1,191 aliases. My solo v13 rerun on the small bank took 242 ms median (versus 356 ms contended). The 5k banks are about 95 to 103 MB each, with peak memory 468 MB for the build and about 190 MB for asking.
findings.implication: For a product, the honest number is about 4 s per question at 5,000 documents on this machine. As frozen, that grows linearly with the alias count, to tens of seconds at 50k. This looks like an implementation cost (memoising named() per question or compiling one matcher would remove most of it), not a limit of the method. The write-up should give the solo number and the reason, and should not compare v13 with v14 on speed.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. Every concrete claim checks out against the saved data and the code.

1. **Contention.** run_5k.sh starts 7 arm processes at once per folder: v1, v4, v8, v9, v11 and v13, plus v12 followed by v14. nproc is 4. Timing is wall clock (`time.perf_counter`, factbank_multi.py:521), so contention inflates it.

2. **The numbers.** Recomputed from the saved answers:
   - md5k v13 (seed 0): median 6,563 ms, total 357.8 s.
   - v13_seed1: median 4,061 ms, max 7,946 ms, total 220.5 s. It ran 08:48:55 to 08:52:36, after every other arm had finished; it is the last ask command in the script.
   - v14 at 5k: median 4,306 ms. It started when v12 finished (08:40:36) and ended at 08:44:16. All other 5k arms were done by 08:41:29, so about 53 of its 220 s were contended and the rest ran alone.
   - Solo v13 (4.06 s) is about the same as v14 (4.31 s). The report's 6.6 s against 4.3 s therefore does not show that v14 is faster.

3. **Mechanism.** named() (factbank/engine.py:123-124) runs one `re.search` per alias with no compiled cache. It is called several times per question (plans.py:170, 259, 441, 442, 482; engine.py:144, 261). The venv's Python 3.12.3 has `re._MAXCACHE=512`.
   - My synthetic probe: 4.6 µs CPU per alias at 300 or 500 aliases, against 54 µs at 1,200 or 3,000. The jump comes from recompiling once the cache overflows.
   - The small bank has 304 aliases, so it stays cached. A precompiled matcher gave the same output at about 0.5 ms per call, against 1.35 ms.
   - The pre-registration estimates about 8,000 aliases at 5k. 8 calls × 8,000 × about 54 µs is about 3.5 s, which fits the roughly 4 s solo median.

4. **What softens it.** The pre-registration already says the time was measured on a shared 4-core machine with several arms running at once (Known limits). It also names the cause: one regex per alias, about 8,000 aliases, about 5 s per question. But scale_report.md lists the contended times with no caveat. It omits the solo seed-1 timing that is in the data, and it invites a v13 against v14 speed reading. The write-up has not been written yet (commit 6266c34: "write-up and review to follow").

So the finding is real as guidance for the write-up: give about 4 s solo, give the regex-cache cause, and do not compare v13 with v14 on speed. It does not affect any accuracy rule, so the verdict that all 5 rules were met stands.

Scratch probes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/post5ka/named_probe.py and regex_cache_probe.py.

findings.title: v1's +0.079 at 5k shows the small bank has its own distortions for content-matching arms
findings.evidence: On the small bank, v1 gives the same wrong answers repeatedly: '2026-03-28' 5 times and 'Confluence spec: ...' 5 times. For example, the three pr_issue due-date questions all get 'due_date of Timezone-aware incremental CSV rollups'. At 5k, v1 finds the right documents for 4 link questions (127, 085, 070, 146/106).
findings.implication: The control isolates size well for planner arms (v13's small-bank answers are right except 067), but it is not a neutral baseline for content-search arms. The write-up should not read v1's gain as size helping.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The evidence checks out, and tracing v1 on the small bank shows how it happens. I saved the trace script and a copy of the small bank's sqlite in scratchpad/post5ka/v1chk/.

1. **The repeated wrong answers are as described.** I compared answers_md5ksmall/factbank.jsonl with answers_md5k/factbank.jsonl. On the small bank, '2026-03-28' appears 5 times and the 'Confluence spec: ...' links answer 5 times. The three pr_issue due-date questions (127, 085, 070) all answer 'due_date of Timezone-aware incremental CSV rollups...'. v1 gains 5 link questions at 5k (127, 085, 070, 146, 106), which is 0.143 to 0.381 on link and +0.079 on the mean. The finding says 4; the true count is 5.

2. **Why it happens: v1's answer depends on whichever document tops the keyword search.** In FactBank.run (engine.py), the PR named in the question gets relevance 1.0. The top keyword (BM25) hit also gets 1.0. The linked ticket is reached one hop later, so its due_date scores lower.
   - **127, 085, 070 on the small bank:** the top keyword hit is dsid_bf412975, a gold document of another question (person_first-060). It carries a due_date, so it scores 9.315. The correct linked ticket scores only 3.214 (written one hop later) and ranks third.
   - **The same three at 5k:** the top hits are dsid_4bfb248d (a Slack 'deadline-extension' message) and dsid_24afb205 (a Gmail message). Neither has a due_date, so the linked ticket wins.
   - **146, 106 on the small bank:** the gold PR is not in the top 5 of a 105-document bank. Another document's creator ties the gold issue's creator at 3.54. At 5k, the PR is the top keyword hit, and the 'open' cue weights author (2.0) above creator (1.9).
   - **So the gain is not better retrieval.** It comes from a bank made only of gold tickets and PRs, where every near match carries the asked field, plus keyword statistics computed over 105 documents. For 127, 085 and 070, v1 had the gold PR at the top on both banks.

3. **No write-up interprets the gain yet.** The pre-registration frames the bank difference as 'the effect of the other documents'. Its Known limits say only that 'the small bank has no unrelated documents', and they do not tie this to v1. The write-up has not been written ('to follow'), so the caution not to read v1's +0.079 as size helping is valid.

4. **Two small inaccuracies in the finding:** the count of gained questions (5, not 4), and 'finds the right documents', which fits 146 and 106 but not 127, 085 and 070. v4 and v8 also move in both directions at 5k (they gain compare_two-160 and -165). That makes the claim that planner arms are cleanly isolated a little generous, but it does not weaken the main point.

**No verdict changes.** v1 is in none of the five rules, and rule 3 uses only the 5k scores of v9, v4 and v8.

findings.title: Changed questions are not grouped by document as the pre-registration promised
findings.evidence: Pre-registration line 137 says 'the changed questions are reported grouped by the documents they are about'. scale_report.json/md lists changed_questions as a flat list with each question's gold_docs, with no grouping. For example, v4's losses on action_owner_issues-110 and -084 (both Maya Chen's four tickets) appear separately, and only -110 changed.
findings.implication: The write-up should add the grouping, using the clusters above, so readers can see that v4's 8 losses are 8 separate clusters and v13's single loss is one PR.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. Line 137 of cie/docs/FACTBANK_5K_PREREGISTRATION.md says "So the changed questions are reported grouped by the documents they are about." In cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_5k.py (lines 445-448), the code looks up each question's gold_docs. The comment there says "to group changes by person or pull request", but the code only adds gold_docs to each entry and builds a flat list in run order. No grouping or clustering is ever done. As a result, scale_report.json "changed_questions" and the matching line in scale_report.md are a flat list of 19 entries. Readers have to compare 32-character dsid lists by hand to see links.

I recomputed the overlaps from part_a/questions.jsonl:
- action_owner_issues-110 (changed: v4 went 1 to 0) shares 4 gold docs with action_owner_issues-084 (unchanged). Both expect Maya Chen's tickets ENG-11024, ENG-250321, ENG-811090 and ENG-99101. A grouped report would show this.
- No two of v4's 8 losses share gold docs: -158, compare_two-159, -110, pr_issue-assignee-113, ticket_link-assignee-130, -122, person_first-008, person_first-060. So they are 8 separate clusters, as the finding says.
- v13's only change, pr_issue-due_date-127, shares no docs with any other question.

One wording flaw: the finding calls -084 a v4 loss that "appears separately". In fact -084 is not in the changed list at all; only -110 changed. That is the very link a grouping would reveal, so the substance holds.

Two things soften it. The commit for the results (6266c34) says the write-up is still to follow, so the grouping can be added there. And gold_docs is in the report, so readers can work out the groups themselves. Still, the saved report does not do what the pre-registration promised.

It does not change the verdict. Grouping only changes how results are presented. All per-arm means, differences and the five rules are unaffected, and grouping makes the result look cleaner, not worse: v13's single loss is one isolated PR question, and v4's losses are independent.

findings.title: v4's -0.06 comes from the questioned people's extra relations, which the small bank lacks; v13's lessons neutralise it
findings.evidence: v4 lost 8 questions and gained 2, spread over 8 clusters. At 5k it chose relations that do not exist for those entities in the small bank. Sofia Patel goes from assignee 2 to also creator 2, and v4 answered via 'creator_of' (DES-35711). For Jordan Lee (0 to 9 meeting attendances, 2 created) it used 'customer_attendees_of -> action_item'. For Maya Chen, Ethan Cole and Luca Moretti it used 'redwood_attendees_of / customer_attendees_of [fireflies]'. For PR 60921 and ENG-87321 it used 'reviewers -> creator_of' and 'creator -> reviewers_of'. Its 2 gains were compare questions it had got wrong on the small bank through other wrong plans. v13 picked assignee_of / linked_linear on all of these.
findings.implication: The write-up can state that 'many more paths for the planner' is a real size hazard, shown by v4. The small control removes the questioned entities' own other relations, not only unrelated documents. Rule 3 holds on either bank (small: v9-v4 +0.264, v9-v8 +0.185).

findings.title: Set-aside questions: v13 consistently answers Linear+Jira; strict 0.443 is not an error rate, and its one lenient 'miss' is the pre-registered second reading
findings.evidence: On all 21 'tickets' questions, v13's answer equals the Linear+Jira reading (lenient 1.0 each). The strict scores are list-overlap partial credit (0.667 to 0.857) or 0 for counts. Of the 2 'linked' questions, -117 is right. For -156, v13 answered Mateo Alvarez via 'referenced_by'. Mateo Alvarez is the assignee of PM-221334, which links to PM-50882, exactly the second reading the 'linked' rule describes. _lenient credits the alternative only for 'tickets', so v13 is right under one reading on 23 of 23. The 21 'tickets' questions cover 9 people (Diego Ramos carries 4 action-owner questions). v11 gives Linear+Jira on 10 and partial on 8; v9 on 9 with 11 'neither'.
findings.implication: The write-up should say v13 applies its trained reading (ticket = Linear or Jira) without exception at 5k. The set-aside score measures disagreement with the generator's Linear-only key, over about 9 people, not accuracy.

findings.title: Confirmed: rules, hash-seed check, reasons and small-bank reproducibility
findings.evidence: scale_report.json gives v13 0.984 on the small bank and 0.968 at 5k, with 'right for the right reason' identical (0.984 / 0.968), so no right answer came from a wrong plan. answers_md5k factbank_v13 against factbank_v13_seed1: 0 answer differences and 0 reason differences. Re-answering v13 on a copy of the small bank (post5ka/smallcopy) reproduced all 50 saved answers and reasons exactly. Every picked question names its start exactly (key, PR number, quoted title or full name). Only 1 of the 20 frozen wordings carries an incidental system word ('status email'). Three person_first subjects with a Jira ticket (Diego Ramirez, Marco Rivera, Jordan Lee) were answered right on both banks, consistent with 'which is due first' not being set aside.
findings.implication: The verdict 'holds at 5,000' (rules 1 and 2), and rules 3 to 5 as reported, stand. The write-up can state them without qualification about the numbers themselves.
